Audio Priority Bar 2.1.0 makes Jabra Link headset detection immediate, decides what a device is from what the device itself reports rather than from its name, and keeps a monitor out of your output lists. Upgrading from 2.0.0 needs no migration, and your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Jabra Link

- Powering a headset off is now noticed in well under a second instead of up to ten. The dongle announces a connect or disconnect about 100ms after it happens, and that triggers an authoritative read of its pairing database. The periodic refresh remains only for an announcement that never arrives.
- Announcements arrive in pairs, so one landing while a read is already running queues another read rather than being dropped, since the first may have seen the device before it went.
- Monitoring is restricted to Link dongles. A Jabra headset or speakerphone plugged in directly can expose the same vendor collection, and it would then have been reported as off despite working normally.

## Device categories

- Outputs are classified from their audio terminal type, so a device that says what it is no longer depends on an English keyword list. This fixes the built-in headphone jack sitting under Speakers on a non-English system, where its name never matched.
- Both value spaces are accepted, since USB and Bluetooth devices report the CoreAudio constants while built-in devices report raw USB Audio codes. Aggregate, HDMI and digital interfaces declare nothing and still fall back to the name list.
- The category a device declares is remembered, so a disconnected device keeps the list it had while connected.
- Jabra Speak speakerphones are treated as speakers. CoreAudio has no speakerphone terminal type, so only the product line settles it. Thanks to [Harinder Takhar](https://github.com/tobi/AudioPriorityBar/pull/39) for reporting this upstream.
- Your own choice still wins over all of the above and persists per device.

## Displays and settings

- A newly detected HDMI or DisplayPort output starts excluded, because a monitor or TV plays sound but is rarely where you want it. Including one by hand is permanent, and **Show all** lists everything excluded. The new **Hide new HDMI and DisplayPort outputs** switch turns the behaviour off for future devices.
- Whatever is currently playing always stays listed, even when excluded, so you can always see where the sound is going.
- Settings descriptions no longer truncate mid sentence, and the window can be resized.
- Settings opens on the screen whose menu bar you used instead of reappearing on the screen you last left it on.

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

The fully qualified command trusts only this cask. Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is ad-hoc signed, not signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
